Recent evidence supports separating recommendation accuracy from actionable usefulness. A 2025 conversational-recommendation study found differences in objective performance without significant differences in questionnaire-based user experience, supporting combined subjective and objective evaluation ([study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0885230824000792)). For this task, a proposed evidence-grounded taxonomy is: **choose now**—explicit immediate intent; **deferred interest**—explicit interest postponed; **explicit rejection**—expressed refusal; **insufficient identification**—available information cannot establish what the item is. Attach supporting feedback excerpts and title/description evidence. These are proposed operational labels, not an established validated taxonomy. Compatibility, ownership, mood, and redundancy remain unknown unless directly supported; missing intent should not automatically become rejection.

Annotation research cautions against treating consensus as unquestionable truth. A 2025 study found disagreement depends on task formulation and annotator choice ([Sources of Disagreement](https://aclanthology.org/2025.comedi-1.3/)). Independently double-code the same feedback, preserve original labels, inspect confusion between deferred interest and rejection, and report agreement before adjudication. The 2026 preprint [Counting on Consensus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06865) emphasizes matching agreement measures to annotation structure, reporting confidence intervals, and analyzing disagreement patterns. Agreement measures consistency, not factual correctness.

[Crowd-Calibrator, COLM 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14141) uses human-label distributions to guide calibrated abstention, with evidence from subjective NLP tasks rather than recommendation. Its transferable principle: preserve uncertainty and evaluate annotation coverage alongside errors among retained decisions. Keep annotator abstention separate from a user’s insufficient-identification response. Twenty users, five per category, provide exploratory cases and failure hypotheses; report counts and supporting evidence, without population-level claims or treating stated intent as observed purchase behavior.
